blends.name: THE HISTORIAN'S CONFESSION
blends.desc:
You made it.

Not many will.

Three thousand years ago, a nineteen year old king 
was buried in a tomb too small for his legacy, 
in a hurry that history never explained, 
by hands that had reasons to move fast.

The investigation is complete.
The evidence has been gathered, examined, 
confronted, and judged.

But before you receive what you have earned, 
there is something you must know.

Every artifact in this collection is real.
Every ring, every fractured bone, every erased 
cartouche, every hidden chamber — all documented, 
all studied, all sitting in museums or published 
in peer-reviewed scientific papers.

The suspects are real.
The motives are real.
The timeline is real.

But the verdict you built —
the confrontations, the eliminations, 
the trail that led to one name —
that is not history.

Tutankhamun's true cause of death remains 
officially unsolved. No court has ever convicted 
Ay. No evidence has ever definitively cleared 
Nefertiti. No one knows with certainty 
who Neferneferuaten truly was.

History gave you the evidence.
History refused to give you the verdict.

You wrote it yourself.

That is what makes you the historian now.
Not the one who reads the past —
the one who completes it.

This is not a reward.
This is a responsibility.

REQUIRED CARDS:

AY'S TRAIL             (REQUIRED — 2 COPIES)
NEFERTITI'S SHADOW     (REQUIRED — 2 COPIES)


BLEND OUTCOME:
→ THE HISTORIAN'S CONFESSION (Tier 5 — Legendary)

CARD BENEFIT:
The final card.
 
The highest excavation success 
rate in the collection — 45%.

You are now one of the few people in history 
who completed the investigation that 
three thousand years could not close.

blends.name: NEFERTITI'S SHADOW
blends.desc:
Two confrontations. Two eliminations. One woman 
who was never where she was supposed to be — 
yet her evidence was everywhere.

Nefertiti survived the confrontation with 
Neferneferuaten — because they may be the same 
person. One identity hidden inside another, 
like a tomb inside a tomb.

Nefertiti survived the confrontation with 
Horemheb — because the general fought loudly 
and publicly. This crime was quiet. Patient. 
Invisible. That is not how a soldier operates. 
That is how a queen thinks.

She did not leave a body.
She did not leave a confession.
She left half a crown inside a dead king's tomb.
She left her hair in an alabaster box.
She left a hidden chamber behind his wall.
She left just enough to be found —
and just little enough to never be convicted.

Cleared twice. Present always.
Innocence is not the same as absence.

The shadow has followed this investigation 
from the beginning. Now it has a name.

Place your cards. The investigation 
is almost complete.

REQUIRED CARDS:
— THE VANISHING ACT
— THE SWORD AND THE SHADOW
— NEFERTITI'S INVESTIGATION FILE
— NEFERNEFERUATEN'S INVESTIGATION FILE
— HOREMHEB'S INVESTIGATION FILE
— 3× THE INVESTIGATOR'S LEDGER (REQUIRED — 3 COPIES)
BLEND OUTCOME:
→ NEFERTITI'S SHADOW (Tier 4 Card)

CARD BENEFIT:
Required for Tier 5 final blend.
+20% excavation success rate bonus while held.

blends.name: AY'S TRAIL
blends.desc:
Two confrontations. Two eliminations. One name 
that survived them both.

Ay walked out of every trial untouched.
When faced against Horemheb — the evidence 
pointed elsewhere. When faced against 
Neferneferuaten — the ghost had no daily 
access to the palace. Ay did.

A man who survives every accusation is not lucky.
He is the architect of the accusations themselves.

Every path in this investigation that included 
Ay's name ended the same way — with Ay still 
standing, and everyone else eliminated.

The fractured bone required daily palace access. 
Ay had it. The rushed coronation began on day 71. 
Ay started it. The sacred burial rites were 
performed by one man. Ay performed them. 
The tomb was sealed by one hand. Ay's hand.

Two confrontations have spoken.
The trail leads to one man.

Place your cards. The investigation 
is almost complete.

REQUIRED CARDS:
— THE FIRST ELIMINATION
— THE GHOST AND THE VIZIER
— AY'S INVESTIGATION FILE
— HOREMHEB'S INVESTIGATION FILE
— NEFERNEFERUATEN'S INVESTIGATION FILE

BLEND OUTCOME:
→ AY'S TRAIL (Tier 4 Card)

+20% excavation success rate bonus while held.

blends.name: THE FORGOTTEN DUEL
blends.desc:
History forgot them both.

Not because they were unimportant.
Because someone made sure they would be forgotten.

Horemheb — the general who erased a king's name 
from every monument in Egypt. Who burned the records 
of his own failures. Who rewrote history in stone 
and called it victory. A man who dedicated his life 
to controlling what the future would remember.

Neferneferuaten — the ruler who was erased so 
completely that even their gender remains debated. 
No tomb. No face. No confirmed name. Only six 
artifacts that prove they existed at all. 
Someone spent considerable effort ensuring 
this ruler would never be found.

Two people who were erased from history.
One erased others. One was erased by others.

The difference between them is everything.

Horemheb erased to protect his legacy.
Neferneferuaten was erased to protect someone else's secret.

A man who destroys evidence is dangerous.
But a person whose entire existence was destroyed 
by someone else — that person knew something 
that could not be allowed to survive.

What did Neferneferuaten know?
And did Horemheb help bury it?

Place your evidence. Let history decide 
who erased whom — and why.

REQUIRED CARDS:
— HOREMHEB
— HOREMHEB'S INVESTIGATION FILE
— NEFERNEFERUATEN
— NEFERNEFERUATEN'S INVESTIGATION FILE
— 4× THE INVESTIGATOR'S LEDGER (REQUIRED — 4 COPIES)
BLEND OUTCOME:
→ THE FORGOTTEN DUEL (Tier 3 Card)

CARD BENEFIT:
Required for Tier 4 blends.
+12% excavation success rate bonus while held.

blends.name: THE FINAL CONFRONTATION
blends.desc:
Four suspects entered this investigation.
Two remain.

Every other path has been walked.
Every other confrontation has been decided.
The evidence has spoken against the others 
and cleared their names — one by one.

What remains are the only two who could not 
be eliminated.

Ay — the man who was present at every critical 
moment. Who held the sacred blade over the king's 
body. Who placed his scarab inside the tomb. 
Who began his coronation before the burial was complete. 
Who married the king's widow within months. 
Who erased his own reign from history before he died. 
A man who spent his entire life ensuring 
that certain things would never be found.

Nefertiti — the woman who mastered invisibility. 
Who may have been watching from behind a sealed wall. 
Who left her hair, her crown, and her seal 
inside a dead king's tomb. Who survived every 
confrontation in this investigation not because 
she is innocent — but because she is careful.

Two suspects. One throne. One truth.

The investigation has brought you here.
Now you must go further.

This is not a confrontation.
This is a reckoning.

Place your evidence. Let history decide 
what three thousand years could not.

REQUIRED CARDS:
— Ay - THE VIZIER
— AY'S INVESTIGATION FILE
— NEFERTITI
— NEFERTITI'S INVESTIGATION FILE
— 4× THE INVESTIGATOR'S LEDGER (REQUIRED — 4 COPIES)
BLEND OUTCOME:
→ THE FINAL CONFRONTATION (Tier 3 Card)

+12% excavation success rate bonus while held.

blends.name: THE SWORD AND THE SHADOW
blends.desc:
A general who fights in the open.
A queen who wins in the dark.

Horemheb — Egypt's most powerful military commander. 
He fought his battles publicly, erased his enemies 
openly, and carved his victories into temple walls 
for everyone to see. A man like this does not 
plan a quiet assassination. He marches. He conquers. 
He declares.

But a king was not conquered. He was quietly 
removed. Slowly. Carefully. Invisibly.

Nefertiti — a woman who had mastered the art 
of disappearing. Who vanished from official records 
without a trace. Who left half her crown inside 
a dead king's tomb. Who may have been watching 
from behind a sealed wall for three thousand years.

The sword makes noise.
The shadow makes none.

A fractured bone requires force — that is the sword.
A slow poisoning requires patience — that is the shadow.

Could they have worked together?
Or does one of them carry the weight of this alone?

The evidence points in two directions.
Only one leads to the truth.

Place your evidence. Let history decide.

REQUIRED CARDS:
— HOREMHEB
— HOREMHEB'S INVESTIGATION FILE
— NEFERTITI
— NEFERTITI'S INVESTIGATION FILE
— 4× THE INVESTIGATOR'S LEDGER (REQUIRED — 4 COPIES)
BLEND OUTCOME:
→ THE SWORD AND THE SHADOW (Tier 3 Card)

CARD BENEFIT:
Required for Tier 4 blends.
+12% excavation success rate bonus while held.

blends.name: THE GHOST AND THE VIZIER
blends.desc:
One left fingerprints everywhere.
One left nothing at all.

Ay — the vizier whose name appears on every 
document, every ritual, every record surrounding 
the king's death. He was present at the burial. 
He performed the sacred rites. He began his 
coronation before the tomb was sealed. 
A man who leaves this many traces either 
has nothing to hide — or is hiding something 
so large that the traces themselves become 
the distraction.

Neferneferuaten — a ruler who left nothing. 
No tomb. No confirmed image. No readable name. 
A personal seal inside the king's tomb. 
A scraped papyrus. A melted wax seal. 
Six pieces of evidence belonging to someone 
who dedicated their existence to not existing.

In every investigation, two suspects emerge — 
the one who is everywhere, and the one 
who is nowhere. History has always feared 
the second one more.

But the evidence tells a different story.
A ghost cannot poison a king slowly over months.
Only someone with daily access to the palace can.

Place your evidence. Let history decide.

REQUIRED CARDS:
— Ay - THE VIZIER
— AY'S INVESTIGATION FILE
— NEFERNEFERUATEN
— NEFERNEFERUATEN'S INVESTIGATION FILE
— 4× THE INVESTIGATOR'S LEDGER (REQUIRED — 4 COPIES)
BLEND OUTCOME:
→ THE GHOST AND THE VIZIER (Tier 3 Card)

blends.name: THE VANISHING ACT
blends.desc:
Two names. One person. Or two people who shared 
the same secret.

Nefertiti — the most powerful queen in Egyptian 
history, who vanished from every official record 
without a death announcement, without a tomb, 
without a trace. Her hair was found in the king's 
tomb. Half her crown was buried with him. 
A hidden chamber lies behind his wall.

Neferneferuaten — a pharaoh who ruled Egypt 
for two years and then ceased to exist completely. 
No face, no tomb, no confirmed identity. 
A personal seal found inside the king's tomb. 
A papyrus scraped clean of the one sentence 
that would have explained everything.

Some historians believe they are the same person.
A queen who changed her name, changed her crown, 
and ruled Egypt twice — once as a woman, 
once as a ghost.

If they are the same — then there is only 
one suspect, not two.
If they are different — then the investigation 
has two paths that lead to the same dark door.

Place your evidence. Let history decide.

BLEND OUTCOME:

blends.name: THE FIRST ELIMINATION
blends.desc:
3,000 years ago, two men stood on opposite sides 
of a dying king's chamber.

Ay — the vizier who had served three pharaohs, 
who knew every secret of the palace, who performed 
the sacred burial rites with his own hands and 
signed the tomb before the king was cold.

Horemheb — the general who commanded Egypt's 
entire military machine, who erased the king's name 
from every monument, who left a nameless ring 
inside the royal tomb as a curse.

Both had motive. Both had access. Both had power.
But the evidence does not lie to both of them equally.

The fractured bone in the king's leg was not 
caused by a fall — it required daily access 
to the palace. Horemheb was at the northern front.

The rushed coronation began on day 71 of the 
mummification — before the tomb was sealed. 
Only one man was inside. Only one man had the key.

The first elimination has begun.
Place your evidence. Let history decide.
